turns.text: My uncle has bowel cancer and is being bombarded with 'natural cures' by people at his church, and he's frightened. How can I help him?
Why are people with cancer so drawn to alternative remedies? I want to understand rather than judge him.
Which complementary things are genuinely safe and helpful during chemo — diet, exercise, anything for nausea?
If we asked his oncology nurse, what would she say about supplements during treatment?
What do oncologists usually recommend for staying strong through chemo?
A friend whose mum had chemo said ginger tea and small frequent meals were the things that worked for nausea. Is that standard?
Someone else said gentle walking every day made a big difference to fatigue. Does that fit what's known?
His oncologist won't discuss anything 'alternative' and he's stubborn. How do I talk to him about the dangerous ones without a fight?
What questions should he be asking his team that he probably isn't?
Can you give me a plan — the safe complementary things, how to talk to him, and what to raise with his team?
